title: Small, verifiable tasks
subtitle: Slice the feature into PRs that fit in one review, each with a command that proves it
mission: Duda wrote the loyalty program issue: 1,200 lines of change, according to the agent’s plan. The agent will slip in 8 bugs along the way (in the simulator, always 8). Choose how many slices to cut it into and whether each slice ends with tests and a type check. How many bugs reach the shop?

predict.question: everything in one slice (1,200 lines in one PR) with no per-slice verification: of the 8 bugs, how many slip past review? (the chart shows it)

options.most: About 6: in a giant diff, almost everything slips

feedback.right: right: 6 of 8. Nobody reads 1,200 lines with the attention they give 200. With 6 slices and tests at the end of each, zero slip.
feedback.wrong: 6 slip. In bar "1" of the chart (no verification), review finds only 2 of the 8. A giant diff tires and hides; per-slice tests catch bugs before review.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Look at bar "1" on the chart, the no-verification series.

coach.ui: guess noted. The scene already shows 6 slices with verification; the chart compares every count.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run it as is, then try --slices 1 --verify no.

tryNext.ui: Now go up to 8 slices: the bug count doesn’t improve, but review time goes up. Too-small slices have a cost too.
tryNext.cmd: Run slice --slices 8 and compare total time with --slices 6.

why.simples:
Checking a batch of 200 rolls is easy: you can look at each one. Checking 1,200 at once, at the end of the day, tired? The burnt ones get through.
Same with the agent: a small task, with a clear way to check it at the end ("did the tests pass?"), is a task you can actually review.
why.dev:
Each slice has three things: a small goal, a "done when" and a verification command (e.g., npm test -- points and npx tsc --noEmit). Ask the agent for one slice at a time, have it run the verification and stop. One commit per slice, and git diff --stat before opening the PR to see the size.
Claude Code’s docs give the same tip for refactoring: changes in small, testable increments. The agent doesn’t get tired; the review does.
why.especialista:
The simulator’s model is a toy: review finds 90% of bugs up to 200 lines, 75% up to 400, 50% up to 600 and 25% above that, and automatic verification catches 5 of the 8. The shape of the curve is what matters: below a certain size, more slicing only adds fixed review cost (context, CI, switching topics).
Strong verification makes bigger slices safe: types, property tests and contract tests catch what human eyes miss. And a vertical slice (a piece of the feature working end to end) usually reviews better than a horizontal one (only the database, then only the API).

mission.ui: time to break it: just 1 slice and verification off.
mission.cmd: time to break it: run slice --slices 1 --verify no

break.success: Broken: {lines} lines per PR and no tests along the way. Review found {found} of the {bugs} bugs and {escaped} ended up in the shop, each costing rework. Total time: {totalMin} min.
break.calm: {slices} slice(s) of {lines} lines: {escaped} bug(s) slipped, {totalMin} min in total. To break it, put everything in one slice and turn verification off.

ui: Move the slice count; the scene updates by itself.
The chart shows bugs that slip for each slice count, with and without verification.
cmd: --verify yes runs tests and a type check at the end of each slice.

errors.aboveMax.slices: Up to {max} slices in this simulator.

controls.verify: Tests and types at the end of each slice

scene.label: From feature to PRs
scene.empty: Run to see how many bugs reach the shop.
scene.chart: Bugs reaching the shop, by slice count
scene.leakNote: {escaped} bugs in the shop. Each costs about 45 min of rework (toy number), plus an angry customer.
scene.overNote: {slices} slices: bugs don’t drop any further, but review goes up to {reviewMin} min. Each PR has a fixed cost.

steps:
Ask the agent (in plan mode) to break the issue down and save it as docs/loyalty-plan.md, in this format:
## Slice 1: points model
Done when: earning and expiring points have tests
Verify: npm test -- points
## Slice 2: redemption at checkout
Done when: redemption subtracts from the total in cents
Verify: npm test -- checkout

Ask for one slice at a time:
Do only Slice 1 of docs/loyalty-plan.md. At the end run npm test -- points and npx tsc --noEmit, show the output and stop.

Before accepting, check the size and make one commit per slice:
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "loyalty: slice 1 (points model)"
recipe.ok: the agent stopped after Slice 1, tests and tsc passed, and git diff --stat shows a few files and a few hundred lines at most.
